semantically_equivalent_models.justification: Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC) involves learning predictive representations through a contrastive loss, aligning closely with the concept of self-predictive representations as both focus on predicting parts of the input data to learn useful features.

The Hierarchical Predictive Coding Model involves hierarchical levels predicting inputs, which is in line with self-predictive representations where models learn by predicting their own input in hierarchical manners.
Adaptive Prediction Sets work with self-prediction to learn representations that can predict outcomes adequately, which aligns with the concept of self-predictive representations.

parent_models.justification: The concept of prediction encompasses self-predictive representations, as predicting future data points or reconstructing missing data parts is a fundamental aspect of self-predictive learning.
Artificial neural networks (ANNs) form a broad category under which self-predictive representations can exist since they utilize the concept of adjusting weights based on predictive feedback.
Feed-forward neural networks are potential architectures used for self-predictive representation learning tasks since they can implement self-prediction through their structured layers.

closest_parent_model.justification: Prediction is the closest parent concept to self-predictive representations because it directly involves the process of a model learning by predicting future states or missing elements, a key aspect of self-predictive methods.

child_models.justification: Contrastive Predictive Coding is a specialized form under the umbrella of self-predictive representations, utilizing contrastive losses to align predictions with learned representations.
As a framework that adapts predictions based on learned data, Adaptive Prediction Sets extend the core self-predictive learning principles to practical set-based prediction problems.

closest_child_model.justification: Contrastive Predictive Coding is the closest child model as it not only adheres to the principles of self-predictive representations but also specifically utilizes a contrastive approach to refine its predictions for learning better representations.

sibling_models.justification: Though not directly involved in self-predictive learning, cross-ensemble representation learning shares the goal of learning robust representations, making it a sibling under the overarching aim of enhanced representation learning.

Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) share learning robust representations, akin to self-predictive methods, but with a distinct sequential learning approach rather than self-prediction.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Cross-Ensemble Representation Learning is the closest sibling model because it directly deals with the concept of improving representation learning, a goal that self-predictive representations also aim to achieve.

unrelated_models.value: discrete abstract representations for transformer-based learning
unrelated_models.justification: While it involves representation learning, the focus on discrete and abstract elements in transformers doesn't align directly with self-predictive representation methodologies.
Self-normalizing networks aim at normalization and stability during learning, which doesn't directly relate to self-predictive aspects where prediction of inputs drives learning.
This model is oriented around conditioning outputs based on returns, primarily in reinforcement learning, which diverges from the self-input prediction framework.
Prototypical Networks focus on few-shot classification tasks, using prototypes for prediction, which stand apart from methods that involve self-predictions for learning.
Variational Autoencoders learn latent variable models primarily through reconstruction, which is a complementary but separate approach to self-predictive methods.
Similar to variational autoencoders, general autoencoders focus on reconstructing data into latent spaces, differing from prediction-based representations.
Supervised learning heavily relies on labeled data for output predictions, whereas self-predictive representations often focus on unsupervised contexts.
These models typically simulate entities with specific rules, generally unrelated to self-predictive methodologies focused on representation learning.
Long Short-Term Memory models are designed explicitly for sequential data, focusing on retaining information across timesteps, distinct from self-prediction driven approaches.
This model is an extension of VAE focused on conditioning, diverging from the self-predictive aim of learning representations through predicting input components.
Recurrent Neural Networks focus explicitly on sequences and memory aspects, typically more connected with sequence prediction than self-representation prediction.
